confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on four web searches of aggregated, crowd-sourced cost-of-living sites (Numbeo, mylifeelsewhere, expatexchange). These gave a mid-range three-course meal for two at about A$150 (A$100-160 range, Numbeo, updated June 2026), an inexpensive meal at about A$20-28, a cappuccino at about A$4.50-5.40 and a domestic beer pint at about A$10.30-12.10. The beer anchor uses a pint-sized pour; a schooner, the common NSW pub serving, is roughly 25-30% cheaper. I found no aggregated current Newcastle prices for cocktails or wine by the glass. Those two anchors are bounded estimates from the local price relationship to beer and typical regional NSW bar pricing: a cocktail is about 1.9x a pint and a glass of wine about 1.1-1.2x a pint, so they are less certain. The accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates only, with no search or listings checked. They assume July (winter, off-peak) and a Newcastle market with limited hostel supply, so the hostel figures are the least certain. The FX figure is the latest RBA observation I found when generating this (18 Nov 2026), not a July 2026 rate. It comes from the RBA exchange rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Newcastle is a mid-sized coastal regional city in New South Wales. One source puts its cost of living at about 82% of Sydney's. Restaurant and drink prices are a little below Sydney and broadly in line with Wollongong, Geelong and the Gold Coast off-peak. Its accommodation is cheaper than Sydney's, with a thin backpacker hostel segment.
